title: 2026-11-05_PACHA_Backdoor_Investigation_043
description: Investigate and respond to the PACHA malware, a Linux server infection that uses coinminers and establishes persistence through various scripts.

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content: The PACHA malware is a Linux server infection that uses coinminers and establishes persistence through various scripts. It communicates with C2 servers and uses iptables rules to manage its activities. Your task is to investigate and respond to this threat.

levels.title: Get Access
levels.cloud_content: You have access to the `target` host with the username `cyrano` and password `cyrano`. From there, you can SSH into `next-target` using the same credentials. Enter 'start' to begin.
levels.local_content: You have access to the `target` host with the username `cyrano` and password `cyrano`. From there, you can SSH into `next-target` using the same credentials. Enter 'start' to begin.

levels.title: Suspicious C2 Service Discovery
levels.content: Security monitoring has detected an unusual network-facing component on the compromised host. Investigate the running services and identify the service responsible for the suspicious activity.
levels.solution:
1. SSH into the `target` host using the provided credentials.
2. List all running and inactive services using the command `systemctl list-units --type=service --all`.
3. Look for any unfamiliar or suspicious service names.
4. The suspicious service is named `python.service`.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Use the command `systemctl list-units --type=service --all` to list all services.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Look for services with unusual names or descriptions.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: The suspicious service is related to network communication.

levels.title: C2 Communication Discovery (Port)
levels.content: An unfamiliar network service appears to be involved in unauthorized communication with an external system. Investigate the service and determine the network port associated with this communication.
levels.solution:
1. SSH into the `target` host using the provided credentials.
2. Inspect the suspicious service `python.service` using the command `systemctl cat python.service`.
3. Look for the `ExecStart` line, which specifies the command launched by the service.
4. The port number used by the service is `80`.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Use the command `systemctl cat <service>` to inspect the service configuration.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Look for the `ExecStart` line in the service configuration.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: The port number is specified as an argument in the `ExecStart` command.

levels.title: Suspicious Data Collection Service Discovery
levels.content: System information appears to be collected automatically without an authorized administrative purpose. Investigate the host and identify the service responsible for this activity.
levels.solution:
1. SSH into the `target` host using the provided credentials.
2. List all timers using the command `systemctl list-timers --all`.
3. Look for any unfamiliar or suspicious timer names.
4. The suspicious timer is named `local-inventory.timer`.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Use the command `systemctl list-timers --all` to list all timers.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Look for timers with unusual names or descriptions.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: The suspicious timer is related to data collection.
